## Source

Adapted from Kameron Decker Harris's Fall 2026 lecture notes
"Contrapositive Proof" and "Proof by Contradiction",
which are typed transcriptions of Scott Wehrwein's Spring 2025 handwritten lecture notes.
These come from those notes:

- the definition of congruence modulo $n$, and the point that it is not the mod operator;
- the human and mammal illustration of a contrapositive;
- the example of a product not divisible by $5$;
- the truth table showing why a proof by contradiction works;
- the outlines of a proof by contrapositive, a proof by contradiction,
  and a proof of a conditional by contradiction;
- the definition and examples of a prime number, and the fact that every integer above one has a prime divisor;
- the statement that $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational (the proof here is different);
- Euclid's proof that there are infinitely many primes.

The exercises are new.

The definitions of the contrapositive, proof by contrapositive, proof by contradiction,
and rational and irrational numbers,
their examples of a proof by contradiction and of rational and irrational numbers,
and the theorem that a conditional is equivalent to its contrapositive,
are included from the
[mathematics prerequisites](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/) notes,
so they read the same in both places.
:::
